transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling really strange and scared. When I’m walking across campus, it’s like I’m seeing everything through glass, or like I’m not completely in my own body. The buildings and students around me feel kind of unreal, and that’s been frightening me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been upset and scared, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed most of the day every day.
Do these feelings of unreality and being detached from yourself happen frequently, or do they come and go? How long have you been experiencing them?

It comes and goes, but it’s been happening enough that I’m really scared by it. Mostly when I’m walking across campus, I suddenly feel like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not fully in my body. The buildings and people around me just feel unreal for a while.
Do these feelings of unreality and detachment happen more often when you’re feeling stressed or anxious about something specific?

Yes, I think it does seem to happen when I’m already tense or worried. But the part that really scares me is when I’m walking across campus and suddenly it feels like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not fully in my own body. The buildings and students around me just feel… not quite real.
Do these feelings of unreality and detachment from yourself ever last for a long time, or do they always go away after a while?

They do go away after a while, but when it happens it feels really unsettling. The main time I notice it is walking across campus — it’s like I’m seeing everything through glass, and I’m not fully in my body. The buildings and students around me just feel a little unreal until it passes.
When you feel stressed or anxious, do you ever feel like you're watching yourself from outside your body, or like the world around you isn't real?

Yes. When I’m stressed, that’s when it seems to happen most. I’ll be walking across campus and suddenly it’s like I’m looking at everything through glass. I don’t feel fully in my body, and the buildings and students around me seem kind of unreal. It really scares me when it happens.
When these feelings happen, do you also experience a racing heart, sweating, or a sense that something bad is going to happen, like a panic attack?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed sweating or my heart racing in a big way. It’s more that I feel scared and unsettled when it happens, but I wouldn’t say I know if it’s like a panic attack.
When you feel like you're not fully in your body or that things around you feel unreal, do you also feel like you can't escape or that something bad is about to happen, like a sudden wave of fear?

I’m not sure I’d describe it as feeling like I can’t escape. It’s more just a sudden, scary feeling because everything feels off and unreal. I do feel afraid when it happens, but I don’t really know if it’s like “something bad is about to happen” exactly.

Do these feelings of unreality and being detached happen only in specific situations, like walking across campus, or do they sometimes come on suddenly without a clear reason, even when you're not particularly anxious?

It seems mostly tied to certain situations, especially when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it scares me the most—like I’m seeing everything through glass, and I don’t feel fully in my own body. The buildings and people around me seem a little unreal. I can’t really say it comes out of nowhere when I’m completely calm.
Do you ever feel like these experiences of unreality or detachment are happening even when you're not in that specific situation, like when you're in your room or somewhere familiar?

I don’t notice it as much in my room or somewhere familiar. It’s really more when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it feels like I’m looking at everything through glass, and I’m not fully in my body… like the buildings and students around me aren’t quite real. That’s the part that scares me.
Have you ever experienced moments where you feel detached from yourself or that the world feels unreal in situations other than walking across campus, even if just briefly?

Maybe briefly, but the main time I really notice it is walking across campus. That’s when it’s strongest—like I’m seeing everything through glass, and I don’t feel quite in my body. The buildings and other students look kind of unreal, and that’s what scares me.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of unreality or detachment even when you're not walking across campus—like when you're sitting quietly or in a familiar place?

Not really when I’m just sitting quietly or somewhere familiar. The part that really scares me is when I’m walking across campus—it feels like I’m watching everything through glass, and I’m not fully in my body. The buildings and students around me seem kind of unreal.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself or that things around you aren’t real, even in small moments, like when you're talking to someone or doing something routine?

Not really during normal conversations or routine things, at least not in a way I notice. It’s mostly when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it scares me—like I’m watching everything through glass, and I don’t feel fully in my own body. The buildings and people around me just seem slightly unreal.
Have you ever felt even slightly detached from yourself or that things around you felt a little unreal, even during everyday moments like watching TV, doing homework, or talking to a friend?

Not really with things like TV or homework, no. I mean, maybe I get distracted, but it’s not that same feeling. The part that scares me is still when I’m walking across campus—like I’m looking at everything through glass, and I don’t feel fully in my body. The buildings and students just seem a little unreal.
Have you ever felt even slightly detached from yourself or that things around you felt a little unreal during moments like walking somewhere else, riding in a car, or just standing in a crowd?

It’s mainly when I’m walking across campus. I don’t really notice it riding in a car or just standing somewhere, but on campus it can feel like I’m behind glass, like I’m not quite in my body. The buildings and students around me seem a little unreal, and that’s the part that scares me.

Have you ever felt even the slightest bit detached from yourself or that things around you felt a little unreal, even in very mild or brief moments, like when you're walking somewhere else, standing in line, or just looking around your room?

I don’t really notice it in my room or standing in line. The main time is still when I’m walking across campus. It feels like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not fully in my own body, and the buildings and students around me seem a little unreal. That’s what scares me most.

Have you ever felt even the slightest bit detached from yourself or that things around you felt a little unreal, even in very mild or brief moments, like when you're walking somewhere else, standing in line, or just looking around your room?

Mostly it’s still that campus thing. I don’t really get it just looking around my room, but when I’m walking across campus, it can feel like I’m seeing everything through glass. I feel not quite in my body, and the buildings and students around me seem kind of unreal. That’s the part that scares me.
